blocks.text: The architecture must keep playback fast and scrolling smooth. Treat this as a client pipeline: feed shell + visibility tracking + prefetch manager + media adapter + playback controller. The media adapter translates feed rendition metadata into browser-supported source selection and preload work; it does not pretend MP4 files provide segmented ABR. The UI is driven by a single active player and a bounded session cache.

Client architecture
- Feed shell + virtualized list
- Visibility observer (viewport + direction)
- Video card component with lifecycle hooks
- Prefetch manager with a measured directional window
- Playback controller (single active player)

Delivery pipeline
- CDN-hosted MP4 rendition candidates
- Choose one supported rendition before an item starts
- Bounded poster and media-session cache
- Retry or choose a lower rendition for a future attempt
- Analytics hooks for playback health

blocks.title: Client media modules
rows: Controls DOM size and scroll performance
Selects supported MP4 rendition and coordinates bounded preload resources
Separates feed metadata from browser media behavior without claiming segmented ABR

steps.title: 1) Fetch metadata
steps.text: Load feed metadata (id, poster, media URLs, duration) and render the first card.

steps.title: 2) Start playback
steps.text: When the first card enters the viewport, the PlaybackController starts playback and records TTFF.

steps.title: 3) Prefetch
steps.text: PrefetchManager schedules a measured directional neighbor window from settled intent, scroll velocity, cache evidence, device memory, and network signals.

steps.title: 4) Adapt quality
steps.text: Before an item starts, the media selector chooses a supported MP4 rendition from device, Save-Data, and recent session evidence. This contract does not claim mid-stream adaptive switching.

steps.title: 5) Cleanup
steps.text: Pause offscreen videos, cancel downloads, and evict cache entries via LRU.

blocks.title: Playback has one owner
blocks.text: You win by controlling the pipeline: visibility drives playback, a small prefetch window drives instant play, and a bounded cache keeps memory predictable.

blocks.title: Media pipeline boundaries
rows: Only the settled card can activate the shared player
Decoded resources can be evicted without losing card identity or anchor
One attempt identity guards source choice, preload completion, and play promises

blocks.title: Viewport-to-playback flow
blocks.text: Make the media path explicit: page intent becomes normalized feed entities, a settled viewport identity, one active playback session, prioritized media work, and finally the rendered card.
Worked example: three fast swipes on a constrained connection

Video A is playing, B is partially buffered, and the user swipes rapidly through B toward C. The frontend must follow the final viewport intent without allowing three decoders, stale autoplay, or abandoned preloads to consume the session.
